title: Klondice: a solitaire roguelike with dice builds. About 70 releases in 12 days, almost all of it written by Claude Code
author: Remarkable_Swing_709
selftext:
Here's Klondice, a solitaire roguelike I've been building.
    
    You play Klondike solitaire against a score target, and the dice in your tray change the rules.
    Each run you build around a card type (Lucky, Gilded, Echo, Combine and more), buy dice from a stall shop between rounds, and the last round of every Set is a Boss with its own rule.
    Clear the whole board and you get a Big Clear, and they stack if you chain them.
    
    
    It's almost all written by Claude Code, directed by me.
    About 70 versions in 12 days, 60 of them tagged in git.
    Unity 6, Android first. Updates are mostly texting my agents from my phone app.
    
    
    How it's set up:
    - Several Claude Code jobs run at once, each in its own copy of the repo on its own branch. Everything lands through a PR with tests on GitHub, nothing goes straight to main.
    - Only one job can ship a release at a time. That lock lives in the job system that runs the agents, not in the game repo.
    - The design bible is the source of truth for the rules. The dice tables in it are generated from the code, so the doc and the game can't drift.
    - I don't trust "done". A verify script checks the PR actually merged, the tests passed and the docs were updated before a job counts as finished.
    - Balance runs as headless bots in Unity's EditMode. 16 builds x 100 runs, about 1,600 runs per check, and it flags anything that moves more than 10%.
    - If a run is in progress when a bug report goes in, the move log goes with it, so a bug can be replayed move by move.
    - The release scripts bump the version, package the build and upload it to Play internal testing with notes pulled from the changelog. It's a few scripts, not one magic button.
    - The big C# files have code maps, so an agent reads the one method it needs, not 5,000 lines.
    
    
    Art is the weak part.
    The pixel art comes from PixelLab and it shows in places.
    
    
    What's still me: the design calls, what feels good and what doesn't, and saying no a lot.
    
    
    Looking for playtesters.
    Unpaid, Android only.
    Every tester gets a free Steam copy at launch.
    If you're keen, DM me the Gmail you use for Google Play and I'll add you. Going the official google internal playtesting route!
    
    
    Any questions about the setup let me know!
